Copy the course's files into your project

Source: R/course-files.R
copy_course_files.Rd

Copies every file listed by sais_example() into a folder of your project, and makes the folder if it is not there yet. After that the files are yours: read them with readxl::read_excel() or readr::read_csv(), as you would a file you downloaded. Nothing is fetched from the internet.

Usage

copy_course_files(to = "data", overwrite = TRUE)

Arguments

to

The folder to copy into. In the course this is here::here("data"), the data folder of your project.

overwrite

Replace files that are already there? TRUE by default, so a damaged copy is easy to repair.

Value

The paths of the copies, invisibly. A message says how many files were copied and where.

Examples

folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "data") # in the course: here::here("data")
copy_course_files(folder)              # copy the course's files there
#> Copied 11 course files to /tmp/RtmpIDBKpQ/data
list.files(folder)                     # see what arrived
#>  [1] "imf-weo-october-2026.xlsx"      "owid_co2_per_capita.csv"       
#>  [3] "owid_renewable_electricity.csv" "wb-country-classification.xlsx"
#>  [5] "wdi_education_spending.csv"     "wdi_electricity_access.csv"    
#>  [7] "wdi_health_spending.csv"        "wdi_life_expectancy.csv"       
#>  [9] "wdi_poverty.csv"                "wdi_primary_completion.csv"    
#> [11] "wdi_remittances.csv"           
library(tidyverse) # load the tidyverse: readr, dplyr and more
#> ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
#> ✔ dplyr     1.2.1     ✔ readr     2.2.0
#> ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.6.0
#> ✔ ggplot2   4.0.3     ✔ tibble    3.3.1
#> ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2
#> ✔ purrr     1.2.2     
#> ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──

#> ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
#> ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors

# Read a saved series from the copy, as you would a file of your own
life <- read_csv(                               # read a CSV file:
  file.path(folder, "wdi_life_expectancy.csv"), # the copied series
  show_col_types = FALSE                        # without the column report
)                                               # close read_csv()

# Join it to the IMF's countries by code and year
weo |>                                           # start with the panel, then
  filter(str_length(code) == 3, year == 2023) |> # countries in 2023, and then
  left_join(life, by = c("code", "year")) |>     # add life expectancy
  select(name, gross_debt, life_expectancy_years) # keep columns to read
#> # A tibble: 197 × 3
#>    name                     gross_debt life_expectancy_years
